wars.summary: The wars of the first years of the Republic, in which the exiled Tarquins enlisted Veii, Tarquinii and Lars Porsenna of Clusium against Rome.

phases.t: Veii and Tarquinii back the Tarquins (Silva Arsia)
Porsenna's attack and occupation of Rome
Arruns Porsenna defeated at Aricia

wars.name: First Latin War
wars.outcome: Roman victory at Lake Regillus; Foedus Cassianum (493) establishes an equal alliance between Rome and the Latin League.
wars.summary: The war in which the Latin League, led by Octavius Mamilius of Tusculum and supporting the exiled Tarquinius, challenged Rome's claim to hegemony in Latium.

phases.t: Latin mobilisation and battle of Lake Regillus
Negotiation of the Foedus Cassianum

wars.name: Volscian Wars
wars.outcome: Roman conquest of the Volscian lands in the Pontine plain and the Monti Lepini; Antium a citizen colony (338), Privernum taken (329).
wars.summary: A century and a half of intermittent warfare with the Volsci, Oscan-speaking highlanders who descended into southern Latium around 500 and took Antium, Satricum, Velitrae, Circeii and the Pontine plain.

phases.t: Volscian offensives and Roman-Latin colonies
Roman counter-offensive (Anxur 406)
Post-sack resurgence; Satricum and Antium; Pontine tribes
Final revolts; Antium and Privernum

wars.name: Aequian Wars
wars.outcome: Aequi defeated on the Algidus (431) and annihilated in 304; Latin colonies at Alba Fucens and Carseoli.
wars.summary: Recurrent warfare with the Aequi of the upper Anio and Turano valleys, whose raids through the Algidus pass threatened the Alban Hills and Tusculum through the 5th century.

phases.t: Aequian raids on Latium; Algidus battles (458)
Roman offensive after Algidus 431; Labici and Bolae
Destruction of the Aequi

wars.name: First Veientine War
wars.outcome: Forty-year truce after the Fabian disaster at the Cremera and Veientine seizure of the Janiculum.
wars.summary: War with Veii for control of the right bank of the lower Tiber and the salt route, remembered chiefly for the Fabian clan's private war and annihilation at the Cremera.

phases.t: Raids and battles
Fabian fort on the Cremera and its destruction
Veientines on the Janiculum; truce

wars.name: Second Veientine War (War of Fidenae)
wars.outcome: Rome captured and destroyed Fidenae (426); twenty-year truce with Veii.
wars.summary: Fidenae's defection to Lars Tolumnius of Veii led to war, the spolia opima of Cossus, and the destruction of Fidenae, giving Rome the whole left bank of the lower Tiber.

phases.t: Revolt of Fidenae; Tolumnius killed
Second revolt and destruction of Fidenae

wars.name: Third Veientine War
wars.outcome: Veii captured and destroyed by Camillus (396); its territory annexed, nearly doubling the ager Romanus; Capena (395) and Falerii (394) submit.
wars.summary: The 'ten-year' siege of Veii, Rome's first great war of conquest, financed by the introduction of military pay and tribute.

phases.t: Siege begins; stipendium introduced
Reverses; Capenates and Faliscans aid Veii; Alban lake prodigy
Fall of Veii; surrender of Capena and Falerii

wars.name: Gallic invasion and sack of Rome
wars.outcome: Roman defeat at the Allia, sack of the city and siege of the Capitol; the Gauls departed with a ransom of 1,000 pounds of gold.
wars.summary: The Senonian Gauls under Brennus, after besieging Clusium, routed the Romans at the Allia and sacked Rome; the Capitol held out for seven months.

phases.t: Siege of Clusium; Fabian envoys fight
Allia (18 July), sack, siege of the Capitol, ransom

wars.name: Gallic incursions of 367-349
wars.outcome: Gallic raids repulsed; peace with the Gauls (c. 331) kept for 30 years.
wars.summary: Recurring Gallic raids into Latium after the sack, remembered for the single combats of Manlius Torquatus (361) and Valerius Corvus (349) and the victories at Pedum (358) and in the Pomptine territory (349).

phases.t: Raids on the Alban Hills and the Anio
Pedum, Pomptine battles

wars.name: War with Tarquinii, Caere and Falerii
wars.outcome: Hundred-year truce with Caere (353); forty-year truces with Tarquinii and Falerii (351).
wars.summary: War with the southern Etruscan cities, notable for the sacrifice of 307 Roman prisoners at Tarquinii (358) and Rome's execution of 358 Tarquinian nobles in reprisal (354).

phases.t: Tarquinian victory and Roman counterattack
Caere and Tarquinii sue for truces

wars.name: First Samnite War
wars.outcome: Roman victories in Campania; treaty with the Samnites renewed (341), leaving the Sidicini to the Samnites.
wars.summary: Short war triggered by the Campanians' appeal to Rome against Samnite attack, fought in Campania (Mount Gaurus, Saticula, Suessula).

phases.t: Deditio of Capua; battles of Gaurus, Saticula, Suessula
Mutiny of the Campanian garrison; peace

wars.name: Latin War (Second Latin War)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; dissolution of the Latin League and the settlement of 338.
wars.summary: The revolt of the Latins, Campanians, Volsci and Sidicini, who demanded equality (one consul and half the Senate to be Latin), and its suppression in battles at Vesuvius, Trifanum, Pedum and the Astura.

phases.t: Vesuvius and Trifanum; Decius' devotio
Pedum and Astura; Latin surrender; settlement

wars.name: Second Samnite War (Great Samnite War)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Samnites renew the old treaty (304); Rome holds Campania, the Liris valley and northern Apulia, ringed by colonies and the Via Appia.
wars.summary: Twenty-two-year struggle for central and southern Italy, begun over Neapolis and Fregellae, notorious for the Caudine Forks (321) and Lautulae (315), and won by a strategy of encirclement with colonies, alliances in Apulia and a military road.

phases.t: Neapolis; Imbrinium; Caudine Forks
Caudine peace; consolidation in Apulia and Campania
Lautulae; Campanian and Ausonian revolts crushed; colonies; Via Appia
Etruscan front; Bovianum; Hernican revolt; peace

wars.name: Etruscan War of 311-308
wars.outcome: Roman victories at Sutrium, Perusia and Lake Vadimon; thirty-year truces with Perusia, Cortona and Arretium; forty-year truce with Tarquinii (308).
wars.summary: Etruscan cities, their truce with Rome expiring, besieged Sutrium; Fabius Rullianus responded by crossing the Ciminian forest into central Etruria.

phases.t: Siege of Sutrium; Ciminian forest; Perusia; Vadimon
Truces; Umbrian campaign (Mevania)

wars.name: Third Samnite War
wars.outcome: Roman victory at Sentinum (295) and Aquilonia (293); Samnites sue for peace (290); Curius Dentatus conquers the Sabines and Praetuttii.
wars.summary: The decisive war for Italy, in which the Samnites under Gellius Egnatius forged a coalition with Etruscans, Umbrians and Gauls that Rome broke at Sentinum.

phases.t: Lucanian appeal; Scipio Barbatus; Tifernum
Coalition; Camerinum; Sentinum
Aquilonia; Venusia; Sabine conquest; peace

wars.name: War with the Senones and Boii
wars.outcome: Senones expelled and their land annexed (colony at Sena Gallica); Boii and Etruscans crushed at Lake Vadimon (283); peace with the Boii for 45 years.
wars.summary: After the Senones destroyed a Roman army at Arretium and murdered Roman envoys, Rome annexed the ager Gallicus and defeated the Boii and Etruscans in two campaigns.

phases.t: Arretium disaster; envoys murdered
Senones expelled; Vadimon
Second defeat of the Boii; peace

wars.name: Pyrrhic War (Tarentine War)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Pyrrhus leaves Italy (275); Tarentum surrenders (272); Rome master of peninsular Italy.
wars.summary: War with Tarentum and its champion Pyrrhus of Epirus, who won costly victories at Heraclea (280) and Ausculum (279), campaigned in Sicily against Carthage (278-276) and was checked at Beneventum (275).

phases.t: Thurii; Tarentine attack on the Roman squadron; Pyrrhus invited
Heraclea; march on Rome; embassies; Ausculum
Pyrrhus in Sicily; Romans recover southern Italy piecemeal
Beneventum; Pyrrhus leaves; fall of Tarentum

wars.name: Picene War
wars.outcome: Picenum annexed; part of the Picentes deported to the Gulf of Salerno; Latin colony at Ariminum (268).
wars.summary: Short war with the Picentes of the central Adriatic, Rome's allies since 299, ending in their defeat near Asculum during an earthquake.

phases.t: Campaign and battle near Asculum

wars.name: Volsinian War
wars.outcome: Volsinii destroyed and refounded on Lake Bolsena; some 2,000 statues taken to Rome.
wars.summary: Roman intervention at Volsinii on behalf of its expelled aristocracy against former slaves or freedmen who had seized power, ending Etruscan independence on the eve of the First Punic War.

phases.t: Siege and destruction

wars.name: First Punic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Carthage evacuates Sicily and pays 3,200 talents; western Sicily becomes Rome's first overseas possession
wars.summary: Twenty-three years of war for Sicily, begun over the Mamertines of Messana, in which Rome built its first battle fleets, won at Mylae, Ecnomus and finally the Aegates, and lost hundreds of ships to Carthaginian skill and Mediterranean storms. Polybius calls it the longest, most continuous and greatest war he knew of.

phases.t: Messana and the alliance with Hiero
Agrigentum and the creation of the fleet; Mylae
Ecnomus and Regulus in Africa
Storms, Panormus and the siege of Lilybaeum; Drepana
Stalemate: Hamilcar at Heircte and Eryx
Lutatius' fleet and the Aegates

wars.name: Mercenary War (Truceless War)
wars.outcome: Carthaginian victory under Hamilcar Barca; Rome exploits the crisis to seize Sardinia
wars.summary: A savage revolt of Carthage's unpaid mercenaries and Libyan subjects that nearly destroyed Carthage after the First Punic War. Rome stayed formally neutral but seized Sardinia at the end.

phases.t: Mutiny at Sicca and siege of Utica and Hippou Acra
Hamilcar's campaigns: Bagradas, the Saw
Defeat of Mathos; loss of Sardinia

wars.name: First Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Teuta pays tribute and is barred from sailing south of Lissus with armed ships; a Roman sphere on the Adriatic coast
wars.summary: Rome's first military intervention across the Adriatic, against Queen Teuta's Ardiaean kingdom after Illyrian piracy and the murder of a Roman envoy.

phases.t: Roman landing and capitulation of Corcyra
Peace with Teuta

wars.name: Second Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Demetrius of Pharos expelled and flees to Philip V
wars.summary: A short campaign by the consuls Aemilius Paullus and Livius Salinator against Demetrius of Pharos, who had broken the 228 treaty, taking Dimale and Pharos.

wars.name: Third Illyrian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; end of the Ardiaean monarchy; Illyria divided into three tributary districts
wars.summary: A thirty-day campaign by the praetor Lucius Anicius Gallus against King Genthius, Perseus' ally, ending with the surrender of Scodra.

wars.name: Gallic War of 225-222
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Boii and Insubres submit; Roman colonies planned on the Po
wars.summary: The great Gallic invasion of Etruria in 225, crushed at Telamon, followed by Roman offensives across the Po culminating in Marcellus' spolia opima at Clastidium and the capture of Mediolanum.

phases.t: Invasion of Etruria; Faesulae and Telamon
Roman offensives against Boii and Insubres
Clastidium and Mediolanum

wars.name: Roman conquest of Cisalpine Gaul (200-191)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Boii lose half their land; Cisalpine Gaul south of the Po under Roman control; colonies at Bononia, Parma, Mutina
wars.summary: After Hannibal's departure the Boii and Insubres, encouraged by the Carthaginian officer Hamilcar, renewed the war. Defeats at Cremona (200), the Mincius (197), Comum (196) and Mutina (193) and Nasica's victory over the Boii (191) ended Gallic independence south of the Alps.

phases.t: Cremona and the Mincius
Campaigns against Insubres and Boii
Mutina and the final defeat of the Boii

wars.name: Istrian Wars
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Istria subdued by 177
wars.summary: Two wars against the Istrians at the head of the Adriatic: a campaign against piracy in 221 and the war of 178-177, ended by the capture of Nesactium.

phases.t: First Istrian War
Aquileia founded
Second Istrian War

wars.name: Ligurian Wars
wars.outcome: Roman victory after eighty years of intermittent warfare; Apuani deported to Samnium; colonies at Luna and Genua secured
wars.summary: A long, grinding series of mountain wars against the Ligurian tribes of the northern Apennines and Maritime Alps, which Livy calls a training ground for Roman soldiers. Highlights include the deportation of 47,000 Apuani (180) and the scandal of Popillius' enslavement of the Statellates (173).

phases.t: First campaigns
Renewed wars; deportation of the Apuani
Final campaigns; Statellates affair

wars.name: Social War (220-217)
wars.outcome: Peace of Naupactus on the basis of the status quo
wars.summary: War of Philip V and the Hellenic Alliance against the Aetolian League, ended at Naupactus in 217 when Philip turned his attention to Italy after Trasimene.

wars.name: Fourth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Ptolemaic victory at Raphia; Coele-Syria remains Ptolemaic
wars.summary: Antiochus III's attempt to conquer Ptolemaic Coele-Syria, ended by Ptolemy IV's victory at Raphia.

wars.name: Fifth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Seleucid victory; Coele-Syria and Judaea pass to Antiochus III
wars.summary: Antiochus III exploited the minority of Ptolemy V to take Coele-Syria, winning at Panium (200); peace was sealed by the marriage of his daughter Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V.

wars.name: Sixth Syrian War
wars.outcome: Antiochus IV forced out of Egypt by Roman ultimatum (Day of Eleusis)
wars.summary: Antiochus IV invaded Egypt twice and was crowned at Memphis, but withdrew when Popillius Laenas delivered the Senate's ultimatum at Eleusis.

wars.name: Second Punic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Carthage loses Spain and its fleet, pays 10,000 talents over 50 years and may not wage war without Roman permission
wars.summary: The Hannibalic War, the defining conflict of Roman history. Hannibal crossed the Alps and annihilated Roman armies at the Trebia, Trasimene and Cannae, detaching Capua, much of the south, Syracuse and Macedon from Rome. Rome refused to negotiate, ground down his allies, won the war in Spain under the Scipios, killed Hasdrubal at the Metaurus and finally carried the war to Africa, where Scipio defeated Hannibal at Zama.

phases.t: Saguntum and the outbreak
Hannibal's invasion: Trebia, Trasimene, Cannae
War of attrition in Italy; Syracuse, Capua; disaster in Spain
Scipio in Spain; the Metaurus
Scipio in Africa; Zama and peace

wars.name: First Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Peace of Phoenice: compromise; Philip keeps Atintania, Rome keeps its Illyrian protectorate
wars.summary: A sideshow of the Hannibalic War: Philip V allied with Hannibal and attacked Rome's Illyrian clients; Rome contained him with a fleet and the Aetolian alliance, then made peace at Phoenice.

phases.t: Philip in Illyria; Apollonia; capture of Lissus
Roman-Aetolian alliance; Aegina
Aetolian peace and the Peace of Phoenice

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Philip evacuates Greece, surrenders his fleet, pays 1,000 talents; 'freedom of the Greeks' proclaimed
wars.summary: Launched after appeals from Rhodes and Pergamon and against initial popular reluctance at Rome, the war ended when Flamininus crushed Philip at Cynoscephalae. The settlement proclaimed at the Isthmian Games made Rome the patron of Greek freedom and the arbiter of the Greek world.

phases.t: Sulpicius Galba's campaigns
Flamininus at the Aous; Achaeans join Rome
Cynoscephalae
Settlement and evacuation

wars.name: War against Nabis
wars.outcome: Nabis surrenders Argos and the Laconian coast but keeps Sparta
wars.summary: Flamininus' campaign against Nabis of Sparta to free Argos, the last war of the Greek settlement.

wars.name: Spanish revolt of 197-195
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Cato pacifies the north-east and organises the mines
wars.summary: A general rising in both new Spanish provinces that killed a praetor in 197 and was suppressed by Cato as consul in 195.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War (War of Antiochus)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Treaty of Apamea strips the Seleucids of Asia Minor west of the Taurus and imposes a 15,000-talent indemnity
wars.summary: The confrontation between Rome and Antiochus III, prepared by years of cold war over Thrace and the Greek cities of Asia. Antiochus' small expedition to Greece was routed at Thermopylae (191); naval victories at Corycus, Side and Myonessus let the Scipios cross into Asia, where Magnesia destroyed the Seleucid army.

phases.t: Cold war: Lysimachia and the embassies
Antiochus in Greece; Thermopylae
Naval war in the Aegean
Scipios in Asia; Magnesia
Treaty of Apamea

wars.name: Aetolian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Aetolians accept a treaty with the maiestas clause and pay 500 talents
wars.summary: Rome's war against its former ally, the Aetolian League, which had invited Antiochus III into Greece: sieges of Heraclea, Naupactus and Ambracia.

wars.name: Galatian War of Manlius Vulso
wars.outcome: Roman victory; the Galatians cease raiding Asia Minor; Eumenes II secure
wars.summary: Manlius Vulso's controversial campaign against the Galatians of central Anatolia after Magnesia, at Mount Olympus and Mount Magaba.

wars.name: First Celtiberian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Gracchan treaties establish a 25-year peace
wars.summary: Campaigns of Fulvius Flaccus and Tiberius Gracchus in the central Meseta, ended by Gracchus' combination of victories and negotiated treaties.

wars.name: Sardinian War of 177-176
wars.outcome: Roman victory; 80,000 Sardinians killed or enslaved
wars.summary: Tiberius Gracchus' war against the Ilienses and Balari of Sardinia, which flooded the slave markets.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; end of the Antigonid monarchy; Macedon split into four republics; Epirus sacked
wars.summary: Rome's war against Perseus, prepared by Eumenes' denunciations. After three years of Roman incompetence and Greek sympathy for Perseus, Aemilius Paullus won the war in a single battle at Pydna (168).

phases.t: Diplomatic preparation; Callinicus
Stalemate; Marcius crosses Olympus
Pydna; Genthius and the Day of Eleusis
Settlement of Macedonia, sack of Epirus

wars.name: Dalmatian War of 156-155
wars.outcome: Roman victory; capture of Delminium
wars.summary: A punitive war against the Dalmatae for attacks on Rome's allies, which Polybius thought the Senate welcomed to keep Italians from softening in peace.

wars.name: Second Celtiberian War
wars.outcome: Peace of Marcellus (152); then Lucullus' unprovoked attack on the Vaccaei
wars.summary: War triggered by Segeda's new walls, marked by Nobilior's defeats (153), Marcellus' negotiated peace (152) and Lucullus' massacre at Cauca (151). The terror it caused led to a levy crisis at Rome.

wars.name: Lusitanian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory after the assassination of Viriathus; Lusitanians settled at Valentia; Gallaecia invaded
wars.summary: Two decades of war in the far west of Spain, notorious for Roman perfidy (Galba's massacre of 150, the bribing of Viriathus' murderers in 139) and for the guerrilla genius of Viriathus, who forced a Roman army to capitulate at Erisane (140).

phases.t: Lusitanian raids; Galba's massacre
War of Viriathus
Brutus Callaicus in Lusitania and Gallaecia

wars.name: Fourth Macedonian War (revolt of Andriscus)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Macedonia becomes a Roman province
wars.summary: The rising of the pretender Andriscus, who reunited Macedonia, killed a Roman praetor and was defeated by Metellus at Pydna (148).

wars.name: Third Punic War
wars.outcome: Destruction of Carthage; its territory becomes the province of Africa
wars.summary: Rome's war of annihilation against Carthage, launched on the pretext of Carthage's war against Masinissa. Carthage surrendered its arms, then refused to abandon its city, and held out for three years until Scipio Aemilianus stormed it in 146.

phases.t: Failed assaults by Manilius, Censorinus and Piso
Scipio Aemilianus: blockade, Nepheris, final assault

wars.name: Achaean War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Corinth destroyed; Achaean League dissolved; Greece under Roman supervision
wars.summary: The brief, disastrous war of the Achaean League against Rome over Spartan secession, ended by Metellus at Scarpheia and Mummius at Leucopetra and the sack of Corinth.

wars.name: Numantine War
wars.outcome: Destruction of Numantia
wars.summary: A decade of humiliation for Rome before the walls of Numantia, a hill town of perhaps 8,000 Arevaci: failed sieges, repudiated treaties (Pompeius 140, Mancinus 137) and the surrender of an army of 20,000, ended only when Scipio Aemilianus encircled the town in 134-133.

phases.t: Metellus Macedonicus
Pompeius and Popillius Laenas
Mancinus' capitulation
Scipio Aemilianus' siege

wars.name: First Servile War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Eunus captured; Lex Rupilia reorganises Sicily
wars.summary: The great slave revolt in Sicily under Eunus ('King Antiochus') and Cleon, which defeated several Roman armies before Rupilius took Tauromenium and Enna.

wars.name: Revolt of Aristonicus
wars.outcome: Roman victory; province of Asia organised by Manius Aquillius (129)
wars.summary: The war that followed Attalus III's bequest: Aristonicus claimed the throne as Eumenes III and raised the poor and slaves of the interior, defeating a consul before his capture in 130/129.

wars.name: Conquest of Transalpine Gaul (Saluvian and Allobrogian wars)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; creation of the province of Transalpine Gaul (later Narbonensis), foundation of Aquae Sextiae (122) and Narbo (118)
wars.summary: Called in by Massalia against the Saluvii, Rome campaigned beyond the Alps for the first time and, after defeating the Allobroges and the Arvernian king Bituitus in 121, annexed southern Gaul.

phases.t: Campaigns against the Saluvii; Entremont destroyed
War with the Allobroges and Arverni
Organisation; Via Domitia; Narbo founded

wars.name: Jugurthine War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Jugurtha captured; western Numidia given to Bocchus, the rest to Gauda
wars.summary: War against the Numidian king Jugurtha, who had seized the whole kingdom and massacred Italian traders at Cirta; marked by Roman defeats, bribery scandals, Metellus' recovery and Marius' victory, ended by Sulla's diplomacy.

phases.t: Cirta massacre, Bestia's peace, Jugurtha in Rome, Albinus' capitulation
Metellus restores discipline: Muthul, Zama, Thala
Marius: Capsa, the Mulucha, battles near Cirta, Sulla's capture of Jugurtha

wars.name: Cimbrian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; the Cimbri, Teutones and Ambrones annihilated at Aquae Sextiae (102) and Vercellae (101)
wars.summary: Migrating peoples from the north, the Cimbri and Teutones with Celtic allies, destroyed a series of Roman armies culminating at Arausio in 105, before Marius, re-elected consul year after year, destroyed them.

phases.t: Noreia; migrations through Gaul; defeat of Silanus
Defeat of Cassius by the Tigurini; Tolosa; Arausio
Cimbri in Spain; Marius trains his army in Gaul
Aquae Sextiae and Vercellae

wars.name: Second Sicilian Slave War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Athenion killed by Manius Aquillius
wars.summary: A revolt of slaves in Sicily, triggered by the halting of manumissions ordered by the senate for unlawfully enslaved allies, created two rebel kingdoms under Salvius (Tryphon) and Athenion.

phases.t: Outbreak; Tryphon king at Triocala; Lucullus at Scirthaea
Servilius fails; Aquillius ends the revolt

wars.name: Social War (Marsic War)
wars.outcome: Military victory for Rome, political victory for the allies: citizenship extended to all Italy south of the Po by the lex Julia (90) and lex Plautia Papiria (89)
wars.summary: The Italian allies (socii) of central and southern Italy, after the murder of Drusus, rose against Rome, formed a state called Italia with its capital at Corfinium, and fought a brutal war that Rome won only by conceding the citizenship they had demanded.

phases.t: Revolt at Asculum; Italian successes; lex Julia
Roman recovery: Asculum, Sulla in Campania and Samnium; lex Plautia Papiria, lex Pompeia
Mopping up; Samnite and Lucanian resistance merges into the civil war

wars.name: First Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Peace of Dardanus: Mithridates gives up his conquests, pays an indemnity and surrenders a fleet
wars.summary: Provoked by Roman envoys, Mithridates VI overran Bithynia, Asia and Greece, massacred the Italians in Asia, and was driven back by Sulla's victories at Athens, Chaeronea and Orchomenus, while a rival Marian army under Fimbria fought him in Asia.

phases.t: Mithridates overruns Asia; the Asiatic Vespers
Sulla in Greece: Athens, Chaeronea
Orchomenus; Fimbria in Asia; Dardanus

wars.name: Sulla's first civil war (Bellum Octavianum)
wars.outcome: Sulla took Rome in 88; in 87 Cinna and Marius retook it and massacred their enemies
wars.summary: The first Roman civil war fought with legionary armies: Sulla's march on Rome over the Mithridatic command, followed in 87 by the expulsion and return of Cinna and Marius.

phases.t: Sulpician laws; Sulla's march; flight of Marius
Cinna expelled; siege of Rome; Marian massacres

wars.name: Sulla's second civil war
wars.outcome: Sullan victory; proscriptions; Sulla dictator
wars.summary: Returning from the East, Sulla defeated the Cinnan regime's larger but poorly led armies in Italy, culminating in the Colline Gate, while Pompey destroyed its remnants in Sicily and Africa.

phases.t: Landing at Brundisium; Tifata; defection at Teanum; burning of the Capitol
Sacriportus, Faventia, Clusium, Colline Gate, Praeneste
Pompey in Sicily and Africa; proscriptions

wars.name: Second Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Pontic victory at the Halys; status quo restored on Sulla's order
wars.summary: An unauthorised raid on Pontus by Sulla's legate Murena, ended by his defeat at the Halys and Sulla's intervention.

phases.t: Murena raids Pontus
Defeat at the Halys; Gabinius brings Sulla's order

wars.name: Revolt of Lepidus
wars.outcome: Senatorial victory; Lepidus dies in Sardinia; his remnant joins Sertorius
wars.summary: The consul Lepidus attempted to overturn Sulla's settlement by force and was defeated by Catulus and Pompey.

phases.t: Lepidus' programme; rising at Faesulae
Senatus consultum ultimum; defeat at Rome and Mutina

wars.name: Sertorian War
wars.outcome: Roman (Sullan) victory after Sertorius' assassination; Spain pacified by Pompey and Metellus
wars.summary: The Marian exile Sertorius, backed by Lusitanians and Celtiberians, held most of Spain for eight years against Metellus Pius and Pompey, and allied with Mithridates, until he was murdered by his own officers.

phases.t: Sertorius establishes himself; Metellus arrives
Pompey's arrival; Lauro, Italica, Sucro, Saguntum
Attrition; murder of Sertorius; Perperna defeated

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Pontus annexed, Armenia reduced to a client, Syria annexed; Mithridates dies 63
wars.summary: After the bequest of Bithynia, Mithridates invaded Roman territory. Lucullus destroyed his army at Cyzicus, conquered Pontus and defeated Tigranes at Tigranocerta, but his army mutinied. Pompey, given the command by the lex Manilia, finished Mithridates, received Tigranes' submission, campaigned in the Caucasus and reorganised the whole East.

phases.t: Bithynian bequest; Chalcedon; Cyzicus; Cabira
Lucullus in Pontus and Armenia: Tigranocerta, Arsanias, Nisibis
Mutiny; Zela
Pompey: the Lycus, Tigranes' submission, Caucasus, Syria, Jerusalem; death of Mithridates

wars.name: Third Servile War (Spartacus' revolt)
wars.outcome: Roman victory; Spartacus killed; 6,000 captives crucified
wars.summary: A breakout of gladiators from Capua became a slave army of tens of thousands that defeated praetors and consuls across Italy before Crassus destroyed it.

phases.t: Breakout; Vesuvius; defeat of praetorian armies
Crixus killed; Spartacus beats the consuls; march north and back
Crassus' command; Bruttian wall; the Silarus

wars.name: Wars against the pirates
wars.outcome: Roman victory; piracy suppressed by Pompey in 67; Cilicia and Crete organised as provinces
wars.summary: Piracy based in Rough Cilicia and Crete, fed by the slave trade and by Mithridates, was fought by Marcus Antonius (102), Servilius Isauricus (78-74), Antonius Creticus (74-71) and Metellus in Crete before Pompey's lex Gabinia command cleared the sea in three months.

phases.t: Marcus Antonius in Cilicia; the law on the pirates
Servilius Isauricus in Cilicia and Isauria; Antonius Creticus' failure
Metellus in Crete; lex Gabinia; Pompey's campaign

wars.name: Catilinarian conspiracy and war
wars.outcome: Conspiracy exposed; five leaders executed; Catiline killed at Pistoria
wars.summary: Catiline's conspiracy of indebted aristocrats and ruined Sullan veterans, with a rising in Etruria under Manlius, was exposed and suppressed by the consul Cicero.

phases.t: Electoral defeat; Manlius' rising; senatus consultum ultimum; Catilinarian orations; executions
Pistoria

wars.name: Gallic Wars
wars.outcome: Roman conquest of Gallia Comata from the Pyrenees to the Rhine; expeditions to Britain and across the Rhine
wars.summary: In eight campaigning seasons Caesar, as proconsul, defeated the Helvetii and Ariovistus, the Belgae, the Armoricans, raided Britain and Germany, crushed a series of revolts and finally the great rising of Vercingetorix at Alesia, conquering all of Gaul.

phases.t: Helvetii and Ariovistus
Belgae
Veneti and Aquitania
Usipetes and Tencteri; Rhine bridge; Britain
Britain; Atuatuca; siege of Cicero's camp
Punitive campaigns; second Rhine crossing
Vercingetorix: Avaricum, Gergovia, Alesia
Mopping up: Uxellodunum

wars.name: Crassus' Parthian war
wars.outcome: Parthian victory; Crassus killed at Carrhae; Parthian counter-invasion of Syria repulsed by Cassius
wars.summary: Crassus' unprovoked invasion of Parthia ended in catastrophe at Carrhae; the Parthians followed up with raids into Syria in 52-51.

phases.t: Crassus crosses the Euphrates and garrisons Mesopotamian towns
Carrhae
Parthian raids into Syria; Cassius at Antigonea

wars.name: Caesar's civil war
wars.outcome: Caesarian victory; Caesar dictator; the senatorial oligarchy broken
wars.summary: War between Caesar and the senatorial government led by Pompey, fought in Italy, Spain, Illyricum, Africa, Greece, Egypt and Asia; decided at Pharsalus (48), with further campaigns against the Pompeians at Thapsus (46) and Munda (45).

phases.t: Italy, Massilia, Ilerda; Curio's defeat in Africa
Dyrrhachium, Pharsalus; death of Pompey
Alexandria and Zela (see Alexandrian War); mutiny in Italy
Africa: Ruspina, Thapsus; Cato's death
Spain: Munda

wars.name: Alexandrian War and the war with Pharnaces
wars.outcome: Caesarian victory; Cleopatra installed as queen; Pharnaces defeated at Zela
wars.summary: Caesar's entanglement in the Ptolemaic succession left him besieged in Alexandria for months; meanwhile Pharnaces II reconquered Pontus, until Caesar defeated him at Zela.

phases.t: Siege in the palace quarter; fire in the harbour; Pharos
Pharnaces beats Domitius Calvinus at Nicopolis
Battle of the Nile; Zela

wars.name: War of Mutina
wars.outcome: Antony defeated and driven over the Alps, but both consuls killed; the victors fell out and Antony returned allied with Lepidus
wars.summary: After Caesar's murder, the senate, led by Cicero, backed Decimus Brutus and the young Octavian against Antony, who besieged Brutus in Mutina.

phases.t: Antony takes Cisalpine Gaul; legions defect to Octavian; siege of Mutina
Forum Gallorum and Mutina; Antony joins Lepidus

wars.name: War of the Liberators
wars.outcome: Triumviral victory at Philippi; Brutus and Cassius dead
wars.summary: The triumvirs, after proscribing their enemies at home, defeated Brutus and Cassius, who had raised the resources of the East, in two battles at Philippi.

phases.t: Bononia; lex Titia; proscriptions; liberators seize Syria and Macedonia
Xanthus, Rhodes; Philippi

wars.name: Perusine War
wars.outcome: Octavian's victory; Perusia burned; Octavian master of Italy
wars.summary: Lucius Antonius and Fulvia, exploiting Italian anger at land confiscations for veterans, fought Octavian and were besieged and starved in Perusia.

phases.t: Confiscations; Lucius Antonius' campaign
Siege of Perusia

wars.name: War against Sextus Pompey
wars.outcome: Triumviral victory at Naulochus; Sextus flees and is executed in 35
wars.summary: Sextus Pompey, holding Sicily and dominating the sea, blockaded Italy's grain until Agrippa built a new fleet and destroyed his at Mylae and Naulochus.

phases.t: Sextus takes Sicily; blockade of Italy
Treaty of Misenum
War renewed; Cumae and the storm of Scyllaeum
Agrippa's fleet; Mylae, Naulochus; Lepidus deposed

wars.name: Antony's Parthian war
wars.outcome: Parthians expelled from Roman territory (39-38); Antony's invasion of Media fails (36); Armenia occupied (34)
wars.summary: After the Parthian invasion of 40, Antony's legate Ventidius expelled the Parthians and killed Pacorus; Herod and Sosius took Jerusalem; Antony's own great invasion of Media Atropatene in 36 failed with heavy losses, though he annexed Armenia in 34.

phases.t: Parthian invasion of Syria, Asia Minor and Judaea
Ventidius' victories: Cilician Gates, Amanus, Gindarus
Jerusalem taken; Herod installed
Antony's invasion of Media; Phraaspa; retreat
Conquest of Armenia; Donations of Alexandria

wars.name: Octavian's Illyrian war
wars.outcome: Roman victory; the Iapydes, Pannonians of Siscia and Dalmatae subdued
wars.summary: Campaigns by Octavian and Agrippa against the Alpine and Illyrian peoples behind Italy's north-eastern frontier, including the sieges of Metulum and Siscia.

phases.t: Iapydes; Metulum; Siscia
Dalmatae; Promona; recovery of Gabinius' standards

wars.name: War of Actium (final war of the Republic)
wars.outcome: Victory of Octavian; Antony and Cleopatra commit suicide; Egypt annexed
wars.summary: War declared on Cleopatra in 32; Antony and Cleopatra were blockaded at Actium by Agrippa and defeated at sea on 2 September 31; Octavian took Alexandria in August 30.

phases.t: Rupture; Antony's will; oath of Italy; declaration of war
Agrippa's blockade; Actium
Invasion of Egypt; deaths of Antony and Cleopatra; annexation

wars.name: Cantabrian and Asturian Wars
wars.outcome: Roman victory; final conquest of the Iberian peninsula, mass deportation of hill populations to the plains, foundation of Asturica Augusta and Lucus Augusti; gold mines of the north-west opened
wars.summary: The last war of conquest in Spain, fought in the Cantabrian mountains and Asturias by up to seven or eight legions. Augustus campaigned in person in 26 BC but fell ill; the decisive work was done by his legates, ending with Agrippa's brutal pacification in 19 BC.

phases.t: Preliminary campaigns of Statilius Taurus and Calvisius Sabinus
Augustus's personal campaign; Vellica, Aracillum, Lancia
Recurrent risings suppressed by Lucius Aemilius, Gaius Furnius and Publius Carisius
Agrippa's final pacification

wars.name: Roman-Kushite War
wars.outcome: Negotiated peace at Samos (21/20 BC): Augustus remits the tribute, Rome keeps the Dodekaschoinos with a frontier at Hiera Sykaminos
wars.summary: Kushite forces under the one-eyed 'Candace' (probably queen Amanirenas) and prince Akinidad took Syene, Elephantine and Philae while the Egyptian garrison was weakened by Aelius Gallus's Arabian expedition. The prefect Gaius Petronius drove them back, sacked Napata and garrisoned Primis, but Augustus settled on generous terms.

phases.t: Kushite invasion of Upper Egypt
Petronius's counteroffensive to Napata
Second Kushite attack on Primis; peace of Samos

wars.name: Augustan Alpine Wars
wars.outcome: Roman conquest of the entire Alpine arc; creation of Raetia, Noricum and the Alpine prefectures; Tropaeum Alpium lists 45 subdued peoples
wars.summary: A series of operations that secured the Alpine passes between Italy and the Rhine-Danube: the destruction of the Salassi in 25 BC, the annexation of Noricum c. 16-15 BC, and the double pincer of Drusus and Tiberius against the Raeti and Vindelici in 15 BC, followed by the reduction of the Maritime Alps in 14 BC.

phases.t: Varro Murena destroys the Salassi
Noricum incorporated; Raeti and Vindelici conquered
Ligurian peoples of the Maritime Alps subdued

wars.name: Bellum Pannonicum (Pannonian War of Tiberius)
wars.outcome: Roman control extended to the Drava and the middle Danube; Illyricum enlarged; Tiberius awarded ovatio (9 BC)
wars.summary: After Agrippa's death in 12 BC Tiberius took over the war in Pannonia, using the Scordisci as allies, and subdued the Breuci and other peoples between the Sava and the Drava, deporting the young men. Velleius and Dio give only outlines.

phases.t: Agrippa's expedition and death
Tiberius's campaigns; Breuci subdued

wars.name: Augustan Germanic Wars
wars.outcome: Rome abandons the attempt to create a province between Rhine and Elbe after Varus's defeat (AD 9) and Germanicus's recall (16); the Rhine becomes the frontier
wars.summary: Twenty-eight years of campaigning east of the Rhine, from Drusus's offensives of 12-9 BC to Germanicus's last expedition in AD 16. By AD 9 a province was being organised, with towns such as Waldgirmes; the loss of three legions in the Teutoburg region reversed this.

phases.t: Drusus's offensives to the Elbe
Tiberius's command; Sugambri deported
Ahenobarbus and Vinicius; consolidation
Tiberius's immensum bellum; fleet on the Elbe
Varus's governorship and disaster
Tiberius and Germanicus secure the Rhine
Germanicus's campaigns of revenge

wars.name: Great Illyrian Revolt (Bellum Batonianum)
wars.outcome: Revolt crushed; Illyricum split into Pannonia and Dalmatia; but Rome's capacity to conquer Germany is fatally weakened
wars.summary: The most dangerous rising Rome faced under Augustus. Triggered by levies for the Marcomannic war, the Daesitiates under Bato and the Breuci under another Bato and Pinnes rose in AD 6. Suetonius calls it the gravest foreign war since the Punic Wars; at its height Tiberius commanded ten legions, 70 auxiliary cohorts and 14 alae.

phases.t: Outbreak; Sirmium and Salona threatened
Battle of the Volcaean Marshes; Germanicus arrives
Surrender of the Breuci at the Bathinus river
Reduction of the Dalmatian strongholds; Bato surrenders

wars.name: War of Tacfarinas
wars.outcome: Tacfarinas killed at Auzea in 24 by Publius Cornelius Dolabella; Roman control of the Numidian steppe consolidated
wars.summary: A seven-year guerrilla war in Africa led by Tacfarinas, a Numidian deserter from Roman auxiliary service who drilled the Musulamii and their Moorish allies in Roman fashion. Three governors won triumphal ornaments without ending it.

phases.t: Camillus's victory
Apronius; Thala
Blaesus's blockhouse strategy
Dolabella; death of Tacfarinas

wars.name: Roman conquest of Britain
wars.outcome: Southern and central Britain become a province; Wales subdued by 78; northern Britain overrun by Agricola to Mons Graupius (83/84) but abandoned north of the Forth-Clyde line within a few years
wars.summary: Begun by Claudius in 43 with four legions under Aulus Plautius and continued by a series of governors over four decades, the conquest of Britain was Rome's largest territorial gain of the first century and a test-bed for client kingship (Togidubnus, Prasutagus, Cartimandua).

phases.t: Plautius: invasion and the south-east
Ostorius Scapula: Caratacus
Didius Gallus, Veranius, Suetonius Paullinus; Mona and Boudica
Consolidation under Turpilianus, Trebellius, Bolanus
Cerialis and Frontinus: Brigantes and Silures
Agricola in Wales and Caledonia

wars.name: Boudican Revolt
wars.outcome: Revolt crushed at the battle of 'Watling Street'; Boudica dies; Iceni lands ravaged; Paullinus recalled after a critical report by the freedman Polyclitus
wars.summary: Rising of the Iceni and Trinovantes under Boudica after the annexation of the Icenian kingdom, the flogging of the queen and rape of her daughters, and the exactions of the veterans of Camulodunum and of Seneca's loans. The rebels destroyed Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before being defeated by Suetonius Paullinus.

phases.t: Outbreak while Paullinus attacks Mona; Camulodunum, Londinium, Verulamium destroyed
Battle and reprisals; Classicianus and Polyclitus

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War over Armenia (58-63)
wars.outcome: Compromise of Rhandeia: the Arsacid Tiridates keeps Armenia but receives the diadem from Nero in Rome (66)
wars.summary: Nero's war over Armenia, fought by Gnaeus Domitius Corbulo, who took Artaxata (58) and Tigranocerta (59) and installed Tigranes VI. After Tigranes provoked Parthia, Caesennius Paetus was humiliated at Rhandeia (62); Corbulo then negotiated the settlement that held for half a century.

phases.t: Corbulo takes Artaxata and Tigranocerta
Tigranes VI installed; Parthian riposte
Paetus's capitulation at Rhandeia
Corbulo's return in force; settlement

wars.name: First Jewish-Roman War
wars.outcome: Destruction of Jerusalem and the Second Temple (70); end of the high priesthood and Sanhedrin in their old form; legio X Fretensis garrisons Jerusalem; fiscus Judaicus imposed on all Jews
wars.summary: The great revolt of Judaea, which began in 66 with the cessation of sacrifices for the emperor and the defeat of Cestius Gallus at Beth Horon. Vespasian reconquered Galilee and the countryside in 67-68; Titus besieged and destroyed Jerusalem in 70; the last fortresses, Herodium, Machaerus and Masada, fell by 73 or 74.

phases.t: Outbreak; defeat of Cestius Gallus
Vespasian conquers Galilee (Jotapata, Gamla)
Perea, Judaea and Idumaea; operations pause for the civil war
Siege and destruction of Jerusalem
Herodium, Machaerus, Masada

wars.name: Civil War of the Year of the Four Emperors
wars.outcome: Vespasian emerges as emperor, founding the Flavian dynasty; Lex de imperio Vespasiani
wars.summary: The civil wars that followed Nero's fall: Vindex's rising and defeat (68), Galba's brief reign and murder (Jan 69), Otho's defeat at the first battle of Bedriacum (Apr 69), and the Flavian victory over Vitellius at the second battle (Oct 69) and in Rome (Dec 69). Tacitus: 'the secret of empire was out, that an emperor could be made elsewhere than at Rome'.

phases.t: Vindex, Galba, death of Nero
Otho vs Vitellius; Flavian rising; Bedriacum II; sack of Rome
Mopping up; Batavian revolt overlaps

wars.name: Batavian Revolt
wars.outcome: Revolt ended by negotiation after defeats by Petillius Cerialis; Batavi keep their privileges; four legions dissolved or reconstituted
wars.summary: Julius Civilis, a Batavian noble and Roman citizen, rose ostensibly for Vespasian against Vitellius in 69 but turned it into a war of independence; Batavian veteran cohorts, Germanic tribes and the 'Empire of the Gauls' joined. The Rhine legions at Vetera surrendered and were massacred, and others swore allegiance to the Gallic empire, the worst humiliation of Roman arms in the first century.

phases.t: Rising; siege of Vetera
Surrender of Vetera; Imperium Galliarum; Cerialis's counteroffensive

wars.name: Domitian's Chattan War
wars.outcome: Roman annexation of the Taunus and Wetterau; road network and watchtowers that grow into the upper German limes; Domitian takes the title Germanicus
wars.summary: Domitian's own campaign against the Chatti, launched from Mogontiacum in 83 under the pretext of a census in Gaul. Tacitus mocked his triumph as a sham with slaves dressed as captives, but archaeology shows real territorial gains and the cutting of 120 Roman miles of frontier roads (limites).

phases.t: Domitian's campaign from Mainz
Fortification of the Taunus and Wetterau

wars.name: Domitian's Dacian War
wars.outcome: Compromise peace of 89: Decebalus a client king receiving Roman subsidies and engineers
wars.summary: Dacian raids across the Danube killed the governor of Moesia, Oppius Sabinus, in winter 85/86. Domitian came in person; his praetorian prefect Cornelius Fuscus invaded Dacia and was killed with much of his army; Tettius Julianus avenged him at Tapae in 88, but the revolt of Saturninus and trouble with the Marcomanni forced a negotiated peace.

phases.t: Dacian invasion; Oppius Sabinus killed
Fuscus's invasion and death
Tapae; negotiated peace

wars.name: Domitian's Suebic and Sarmatian Wars
wars.outcome: Sarmatians defeated by 93 (Domitian's ovatio, laurel only); fighting with the Suebi continues into 97 when Nerva takes the title Germanicus
wars.summary: The Marcomanni and Quadi refused aid against Dacia and were attacked in 89; in 92 the Iazyges with Suebic allies destroyed legio XXI Rapax. Domitian took the field himself in Pannonia (92-93).

phases.t: Punitive campaign against Marcomanni and Quadi
Iazyges invasion; XXI Rapax destroyed; Domitian in Pannonia
Suebic war concluded under Nerva

wars.name: First Dacian War
wars.outcome: Decebalus submits: surrenders arms, engineers and deserters, demolishes forts, cedes territory (Banat, Oltenia); Roman garrison at Sarmizegetusa
wars.summary: Trajan's first war against Decebalus, launched in March 101 with perhaps nine legions and as many auxiliaries. After a costly victory at Tapae, a Dacian and Roxolanian counterattack into Moesia in winter 101/102, and a converging advance on the Orăștie mountains, Decebalus sued for peace.

phases.t: Crossing at Lederata; advance on Tapae
Dacian-Roxolanian raid on Moesia; battle near Adamclisi
Assault on the Orăștie mountain fortresses; peace

wars.name: Second Dacian War
wars.outcome: Dacian kingdom destroyed; Decebalus's suicide; province of Dacia created; vast booty
wars.summary: Decebalus rearmed, attacked Roman garrisons, captured the commander Longinus and tried to assassinate Trajan. Trajan crossed by his new stone bridge at Drobeta, besieged Sarmizegetusa Regia in summer 106 and hunted down the king, whose head was displayed on the Gemonian stairs.

phases.t: Dacian offensive; Trajan returns
Siege of Sarmizegetusa; death of Decebalus; annexation

wars.name: Trajan's Parthian War
wars.outcome: Armenia, Mesopotamia and Assyria briefly annexed, Ctesiphon taken and a client king installed; massive revolts and the Jewish diaspora rising force retreat; Hadrian abandons the conquests in 117
wars.summary: Provoked by Osroes I's deposition of the Armenian king Axidares, Trajan annexed Armenia in 114, conquered northern Mesopotamia in 115 and marched down the Euphrates to Ctesiphon and the Persian Gulf in 116. Revolts across the new provinces and a failed siege of Hatra ended the enterprise.

phases.t: Annexation of Armenia
Northern Mesopotamia; Antioch earthquake
Ctesiphon and the Gulf; revolts
Siege of Hatra; Trajan's death

wars.name: Diaspora Revolt (Kitos War)
wars.outcome: Jewish communities of Cyrenaica, Egypt and Cyprus destroyed or reduced to insignificance; Jews banned from Cyprus
wars.summary: Simultaneous Jewish uprisings in Cyrenaica, Egypt, Cyprus and Mesopotamia while Trajan was campaigning in Parthia. Dio claims 220,000 killed in Cyrene and 240,000 in Cyprus; papyri and inscriptions confirm widespread devastation in Egypt and Cyrene.

phases.t: Risings in Cyrene, Egypt, Cyprus
Mesopotamia; suppression by Turbo and Quietus

wars.name: Bar Kokhba Revolt
wars.outcome: Revolt crushed with enormous loss of life; Jerusalem refounded as Aelia Capitolina and closed to Jews; Judaea renamed Syria Palaestina
wars.summary: The second great Jewish revolt, led by Simon bar Kosiba, hailed by Rabbi Akiva as 'Bar Kokhba' (son of the star). Rome had to bring Sextus Julius Severus from Britain and units from across the empire; Hadrian omitted the customary 'I and the army are well' from his letter to the Senate.

phases.t: Outbreak; rebels control Judaean hill country
Julius Severus's war of attrition; fall of Betar
Mopping up in the Judaean desert caves

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of Lucius Verus
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Armenia restored to a Roman client, Osroene and Dura-Europos under Roman control, Seleucia and Ctesiphon sacked; but returning troops spread the Antonine Plague
wars.summary: Vologases IV invaded Armenia in 161, destroyed a Roman army at Elegeia and defeated the governor of Syria. Lucius Verus was sent east; his generals Statius Priscus, Avidius Cassius and Martius Verus won the war while Verus stayed mostly at Antioch and Daphne.

phases.t: Parthian invasion; Elegeia
Reconquest of Armenia
Mesopotamian offensive; Seleucia and Ctesiphon
Media; triumph in Rome

wars.name: Marcomannic Wars
wars.outcome: Rome restores the Danube frontier after near-catastrophe; Marcus's plans for provinces of Marcomannia and Sarmatia abandoned by Commodus in the peace of 180
wars.summary: A generation of war along the middle Danube, beginning with an incursion of Langobardi and Obii in 166/167 and culminating in the first barbarian invasion of Italy for nearly three centuries, when Marcomanni and Quadi besieged Aquileia and destroyed Opitergium. Marcus Aurelius spent most of his last decade at Carnuntum, Sirmium and Vindobona, writing the Meditations.

phases.t: Incursions; Marcus and Verus go north
Failed Roman offensive; invasion of Italy; Costoboci raid Greece
Campaigns against Marcomanni, Quadi, Iazyges; Rain Miracle
Second expedition; Roman garrisons in Quadi lands; death of Marcus

wars.name: Civil wars of 193-197
wars.outcome: Septimius Severus defeats Didius Julianus (193), Pescennius Niger (194) and Clodius Albinus (197) and founds the Severan dynasty
wars.summary: The wars of succession after the murder of Pertinax, in which the Danubian army's candidate Septimius Severus defeated the Syrian army's Pescennius Niger and then the British army's Clodius Albinus.

phases.t: Julianus overthrown; Severus takes Rome
War against Niger: Cyzicus, Nicaea, Issus
Siege of Byzantium
War against Albinus: Lugdunum

wars.name: Parthian wars of Septimius Severus
wars.outcome: Roman victory; sack of Ctesiphon; creation of the province of Mesopotamia; Hatra unconquered
wars.summary: Severus' two eastern wars: a punitive campaign of 195 against Osroene and Adiabene, and the invasion of 197-198 that sacked Ctesiphon, followed by two failed sieges of Hatra.

phases.t: Campaign against Osroene and Adiabene
Invasion of Babylonia; sack of Ctesiphon
Sieges of Hatra

wars.name: Severus' Caledonian war
wars.outcome: Inconclusive; Caledonians and Maeatae submit and revolt; Caracalla withdraws to Hadrian's Wall after Severus' death
wars.summary: The imperial expedition of Severus, Caracalla and Geta against the Caledonii and Maeatae beyond the Antonine line, based at York, with a legionary base at Carpow on the Tay.

phases.t: Arrival and first campaign; submission of the Caledonians
Revolt and genocidal punitive campaign
Severus dies; Caracalla makes peace

wars.name: Parthian war of Caracalla and Macrinus
wars.outcome: Indecisive; Macrinus pays Artabanus IV 200 million sesterces
wars.summary: Caracalla's invasion of Media and Adiabene after his marriage proposal was refused, ended by his murder and by Macrinus' bloody draw at Nisibis.

phases.t: Caracalla's raid into Media; tombs at Arbela desecrated
Caracalla murdered; battle of Nisibis; peace

wars.name: First Sasanian war (Ardashir and Severus Alexander)
wars.outcome: Stalemate; Mesopotamia preserved at heavy cost
wars.summary: The first war between Rome and the new Sasanian dynasty: Ardashir's invasion of Mesopotamia and Alexander's three-column counter-offensive of 232.

wars.name: German war of Severus Alexander and Maximinus
wars.outcome: Roman punitive victories, including the battle at the Harzhorn; Maximinus takes the title Germanicus Maximus
wars.summary: Campaigns on the Rhine against Germanic incursions of 233-234, begun by Severus Alexander (murdered at Mogontiacum) and carried deep into Germany by Maximinus, then continued on the Danube against Sarmatians and Dacians.

wars.name: Civil war of 238 (Year of the Six Emperors)
wars.outcome: Maximinus killed at Aquileia; Pupienus and Balbinus murdered; Gordian III sole emperor
wars.summary: The Senate's rebellion against Maximinus Thrax, begun by the Gordians' revolt in Africa and ending with the Praetorians installing Gordian III.

phases.t: Gordians proclaimed at Thysdrus; defeated at Carthage
Pupienus and Balbinus; siege of Aquileia
Praetorians murder the senatorial emperors

wars.name: Persian war of Gordian III
wars.outcome: Persian victory at Misiche; Gordian III dies; Philip pays 500,000 aurei
wars.summary: After the Sasanians took Hatra, Nisibis and Carrhae, Gordian III's great expedition won at Rhesaina but was defeated at Misiche; Philip the Arab made peace.

wars.name: Gothic war of Decius
wars.outcome: Gothic victory; Decius killed at Abritus; Gallus pays tribute
wars.summary: The invasion of Moesia and Thrace by Cniva's Goths and their allies, culminating in the sack of Philippopolis and the death of Decius at Abritus.

wars.name: Shapur I's second and third wars against Rome
wars.outcome: Sasanian victories: Barbalissos, Antioch sacked, Dura destroyed, Valerian captured; Odaenathus' counter-offensives restore the Roman East
wars.summary: Shapur I's devastating invasions of Syria, Cappadocia and Cilicia, including the capture of Valerian at Edessa in 260, followed by Odaenathus of Palmyra's counterattacks to Ctesiphon.

phases.t: Second campaign: Barbalissos, sack of Antioch, Dura-Europos
Third campaign: Edessa and capture of Valerian; raids into Cilicia and Cappadocia
Odaenathus' counter-offensives

wars.name: Gothic and Herulian invasions
wars.outcome: After two decades of raids by land and sea, Roman victories at the Nestus, Naissus and beyond the Danube end the great invasions
wars.summary: Seaborne raids by Boranoi, Goths and Heruli across the Black Sea and Aegean (Pityus, Trapezus, Bithynia, Athens), and land invasions of the Balkans, ended by Gallienus, Claudius II and Aurelian.

phases.t: Black Sea raids: Pityus, Trapezus, Bithynia
Great Herulian raid; Athens sacked
Naissus and pursuit
Aurelian's victory beyond the Danube

wars.name: Alamannic and Juthungian invasions of Italy
wars.outcome: Invaders defeated at Milan (259), Lake Benacus (268), Fano and Pavia (271) after a defeat at Placentia
wars.summary: Repeated invasions of Italy by Alamanni and Juthungi through the Alpine passes, prompting the building of the Aurelian Walls.

wars.name: Wars against the Gallic Empire
wars.outcome: Aurelian defeats Tetricus at Châlons (274); Gaul, Britain and Spain reunited with the empire
wars.summary: The secession of the western provinces under Postumus, Victorinus and Tetricus, intermittent Roman attempts to recover them, and Aurelian's reconquest.

phases.t: Postumus' secession; Gallienus' failed recovery
Laelianus, Marius, Victorinus; Autun sacked
Aurelian's reconquest at Châlons

wars.name: Palmyrene war
wars.outcome: Aurelian conquers Palmyra; Zenobia captured; Palmyra sacked after a second revolt
wars.summary: Zenobia's expansion into Egypt and Asia Minor and Aurelian's reconquest of the East in 272, with the second revolt and sack of Palmyra in 273.

phases.t: Palmyrene conquest of Egypt and Asia Minor
Aurelian's campaign: Tyana, Immae, Emesa, siege of Palmyra
Second revolt; sack of Palmyra; Firmus in Egypt

wars.name: Carausian revolt
wars.outcome: Constantius I recovers Britain after the defeat of Allectus
wars.summary: The ten-year secession of Britain and parts of northern Gaul under Carausius and Allectus, ended by Constantius' capture of Boulogne (293) and the invasion of 296.

wars.name: Persian war of Galerius and Narseh
wars.outcome: Decisive Roman victory; Peace of Nisibis gives Rome five Transtigritane regions and control of Armenia and Iberia
wars.summary: Narseh's invasion of Armenia and Mesopotamia, Galerius' defeat near Callinicum, and his crushing victory in Armenia in 298 followed by the Peace of Nisibis.

wars.name: Civil wars of the Tetrarchy
wars.outcome: Collapse of the tetrarchic system; Constantine controls the West and Licinius the East by 313
wars.summary: The struggles following the abdications of 305: the usurpations of Constantine and Maxentius (306), the failures of Severus and Galerius in Italy (307), the Carnuntum settlement (308), the fall of Maximian (310), Constantine's conquest of Italy (312) and Licinius' defeat of Maximinus Daia (313).

phases.t: Usurpations of Constantine and Maxentius; Severus and Galerius fail in Italy
Carnuntum settlement; Domitius Alexander; Maximian's end
Constantine invades Italy: Turin, Verona, Milvian Bridge
Licinius defeats Maximinus Daia

wars.name: Wars of Constantine and Licinius
wars.outcome: Constantine sole emperor after Chrysopolis (324); Licinius executed (325)
wars.summary: Two wars between the Augusti: the first (316-317) gave Constantine the Balkans after Cibalae and Mardia; the second (324), presented by Eusebius as a holy war, ended with Adrianople, the Hellespont and Chrysopolis.

phases.t: First war: Cibalae, Mardia; peace of Serdica
Second war: Adrianople, Hellespont, Chrysopolis

wars.name: Constantine's Gothic and Sarmatian war
wars.outcome: Roman victory; treaty of 332 with the Tervingi; settlement of Sarmatian refugees
wars.summary: Constantine's reassertion of Roman power north of the lower Danube: the bridge at Oescus (328), Constantine II's victory over the Tervingi (332), the ensuing treaty and the reception of 300,000 Sarmatians (334).

wars.name: Persian war of Constantius II and Shapur II
wars.outcome: Stalemate for two decades; Shapur takes Amida, Singara and Bezabde (359-360)
wars.summary: A long war of sieges and raids in northern Mesopotamia: Shapur's three sieges of Nisibis (338, 346, 350), the night battle of Singara (344 or 348), and his offensive of 359-360 that took Amida, Singara and Bezabde.

phases.t: Sieges of Nisibis; Singara
Truce in practice; Shapur fights in the east, Constantius in the west
Shapur's offensive: Amida, Singara, Bezabde

wars.name: Civil war against Magnentius
wars.outcome: Constantius II defeats Magnentius at Mursa and Mons Seleucus; sole emperor
wars.summary: The usurpation of Magnentius in the West after the murder of Constans, the brief reigns of Vetranio and Nepotianus, and Constantius' victory at Mursa (351), one of the bloodiest battles of Roman history.

wars.name: Julian's Alamannic and Frankish wars
wars.outcome: Rhine frontier restored; Chnodomar captured at Strasbourg; Frankish Salii settled in Toxandria
wars.summary: Julian's campaigns as Caesar in Gaul: relief of Cologne and Autun, the victory of Strasbourg (357), crossings of the Rhine, and treaties with Alamannic and Frankish kings.

wars.name: Julian's Persian expedition
wars.outcome: Julian killed; Jovian cedes Nisibis, Singara and the Transtigritane regions
wars.summary: Julian's invasion of Persia with perhaps 65,000 men down the Euphrates to Ctesiphon, his death during the retreat, and Jovian's humiliating peace.

wars.name: Revolt of Procopius
wars.outcome: Procopius defeated at Thyatira and Nacolia and executed
wars.summary: The usurpation of Julian's relative Procopius at Constantinople, supported by Gothic troops, against Valens.

wars.name: Valens' Gothic war
wars.outcome: Treaty on the Danube between Valens and Athanaric; subsidies ended and trade restricted
wars.summary: Valens' punitive campaigns north of the Danube against the Tervingi who had supported Procopius.

wars.name: Revolt of Firmus
wars.outcome: Count Theodosius suppresses the revolt; Firmus commits suicide
wars.summary: The rebellion of the Moorish prince Firmus in Mauretania, provoked by the abuses of the comes Africae Romanus.

wars.name: Quadic and Sarmatian war
wars.outcome: Roman punitive campaign; Valentinian I dies at Brigetio
wars.summary: Invasion of Pannonia by the Quadi and Sarmatians after the murder of the Quadic king Gabinius, answered by Valentinian's campaign of 375.

wars.name: Gothic war of 376-382
wars.outcome: Roman catastrophe at Adrianople; treaty of 382 settles the Goths within the empire as an autonomous people
wars.summary: The war that began when Tervingian refugees from the Huns, abused by Roman officials, revolted in Thrace; it brought the death of Valens and most of the eastern field army at Adrianople and ended with Theodosius' treaty of 382.

phases.t: Crossing of the Danube; Marcianople; Ad Salices
Argentaria; Adrianople; Goths fail before Constantinople
Theodosius' war of containment; treaty of 3 October 382

wars.name: Civil war against Magnus Maximus
wars.outcome: Theodosius defeats Maximus at Siscia and Poetovio; Maximus executed at Aquileia
wars.summary: Magnus Maximus' usurpation in Britain and Gaul (383), uneasy recognition (384-387), invasion of Italy (387) and defeat by Theodosius (388).

wars.name: Civil war against Eugenius
wars.outcome: Theodosius wins at the Frigidus; Eugenius executed and Arbogast commits suicide
wars.summary: Following the death of Valentinian II, Arbogast's emperor Eugenius held the West for two years with pagan senatorial support until Theodosius' victory at the Frigidus.

wars.name: Gothic Wars of Alaric and his successors
wars.outcome: Goths settled as federates in Aquitaine (418) after sacking Rome (410); the Visigothic kingdom of Toulouse is born
wars.summary: Twenty-three years of intermittent war, negotiation and alliance between the Goths led by Alaric, Athaulf and Wallia and the two Roman courts, from the revolt of 395 to the settlement in Aquitaine.

phases.t: Revolt in the Balkans and ravaging of Greece
First invasion of Italy: Pollentia and Verona
Sieges and sack of Rome
Athaulf in Gaul and Spain
Wallia as Roman federate in Spain; settlement in Aquitaine

wars.name: Gildonic War
wars.outcome: Gildo defeated and killed; Africa and its grain restored to the western court
wars.summary: Gildo, comes Africae, transferred Africa to the eastern court and cut Rome's grain. Stilicho sent Gildo's brother Mascezel, who routed him at the Ardalio.

wars.name: Invasion of Radagaisus
wars.outcome: Radagaisus's host destroyed at Faesulae; 12,000 drafted into the Roman army
wars.summary: A Gothic-led coalition from the middle Danube invaded Italy and was annihilated by Stilicho with Hunnic and Gothic auxiliaries.

wars.name: Usurpation of Constantine III
wars.outcome: Constantine III defeated and executed; Gaul restored to Ravenna, Britain lost
wars.summary: Civil war between Honorius and the British-born usurper Constantine III, complicated by the rebellion of Constantine's general Gerontius and his emperor Maximus in Spain, and by the Rhine invaders.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 421-422
wars.outcome: Status quo; mutual religious toleration and no new frontier forts
wars.summary: Brief war triggered by Bahram V's persecution of Christians and Roman refusal to return refugees.

wars.name: War against Joannes
wars.outcome: Joannes executed; Valentinian III installed with Galla Placidia as regent
wars.summary: Theodosius II's intervention to install his cousin Valentinian III against the Ravenna usurper Joannes, who was backed by Aetius and his Huns.

wars.name: Vandal conquest of Africa
wars.outcome: Vandals take Carthage (439); treaty of 442 recognises their rule over the richest provinces
wars.summary: The Vandals and Alans under Gaiseric crossed to Africa, besieged Hippo, defeated Roman and eastern armies, were recognised as federates in 435, and seized Carthage in 439.

wars.name: Aetius's wars in Gaul
wars.outcome: Burgundians crushed and resettled; Visigoths contained after the defeat of Litorius
wars.summary: Aetius's campaigns, often with Hunnic auxiliaries, against Visigoths at Arles and Narbonne, Franks on the Rhine, Burgundians, Iuthungi and the Bagaudae of Armorica.

wars.name: Wars with Attila's Huns
wars.outcome: Huge tribute extracted from the East; Attila halted in Gaul (451), withdrew from Italy (452); Hunnic empire collapses after Nedao (454)
wars.summary: Two decades of Hunnic pressure: treaties and rising tribute (435, 443, 447), devastating Balkan invasions (441-442, 447), the invasion of Gaul (451) and Italy (452), and the collapse after Attila's death.

phases.t: Treaties of Margus and rising tribute
Balkan invasions
Diplomacy and the Honoria affair
Invasions of Gaul and Italy
Death of Attila and Nedao

wars.name: Roman-Vandal War of 455-474
wars.outcome: Both Roman counter-offensives (460, 468) fail; Zeno recognises Vandal rule in perpetual peace (474)
wars.summary: After the sack of Rome, twenty years of Vandal naval raiding on Italy, Sicily and the Aegean, and two great Roman attempts at reconquest under Majorian and Basiliscus, both destroyed before landing in force.

wars.name: Revolt of Illus
wars.outcome: Illus and Leontius defeated and executed
wars.summary: Rebellion of Zeno's Isaurian minister Illus with the usurper Leontius and the dowager Verina, ending with the four-year siege of Papyrius.

wars.name: Ostrogothic conquest of Italy
wars.outcome: Odoacer killed; Theodoric rules Italy
wars.summary: Theodoric the Amal, commissioned by Zeno, led the Goths from the Balkans into Italy and in four years of war destroyed Odoacer's regime.

wars.name: Isaurian War
wars.outcome: Isaurian resistance crushed; many deported to Thrace
wars.summary: Anastasius's war against the Isaurian faction expelled from Constantinople after Zeno's death, decided at Cotyaeum and ended by the capture of their mountain strongholds.

wars.name: Anastasian War
wars.outcome: Seven-year truce; Romans recover Amida by payment and build Dara
wars.summary: Kavad I's invasion to extort money, notable for the siege of Amida, poor Roman command coordination, and the building of Dara.

wars.name: Frankish-Visigothic War
wars.outcome: Visigoths lose almost all of Gaul; Ostrogoths secure Septimania and Provence
wars.summary: Clovis's attack on the Visigothic kingdom of Toulouse, decided at Vouillé, with Theodoric's Ostrogoths intervening in 508 to save Septimania.

wars.name: Revolt of Vitalian
wars.outcome: Vitalian's fleet destroyed (515); he is later rehabilitated by Justin I
wars.summary: Three marches on Constantinople by the Thracian federate commander Vitalian, demanding Chalcedonian orthodoxy and pay for the federates.

wars.name: Iberian War
wars.outcome: 'Eternal Peace' (532): status quo, Rome pays 11,000 lbs of gold
wars.summary: War sparked by the revolt of the Iberian king Gourgen against Persia, fought in Lazica, Armenia and Mesopotamia. Belisarius won at Dara and lost at Callinicum.

wars.name: Vandalic War
wars.outcome: Vandal kingdom destroyed; Africa, Sardinia, Corsica and the Balearics reconquered
wars.summary: Belisarius's lightning campaign that destroyed the Vandal kingdom in two battles and restored Roman rule in Africa after 94 years.

wars.name: Moorish Wars in Roman Africa
wars.outcome: Moorish coalition broken at the Campi Catonis; fifteen years of peace
wars.summary: Fourteen years of war against the Mauri of Byzacena, Numidia and Tripolitania, interwoven with military mutinies (Stotzas 536, Guntharic 545-546). Solomon was killed in 544; John Troglita won the final victory in 548.

wars.name: Gothic War
wars.outcome: Ostrogothic kingdom destroyed; Italy reconquered but devastated; Pragmatic Sanction (554)
wars.summary: Justinian's twenty-year war to recover Italy: Belisarius's rapid conquest (535-540), Totila's revival (541-550), and Narses's final victories (551-554), with Frankish interventions throughout.

phases.t: Belisarius's conquest: Sicily, Naples, siege of Rome, Ravenna
Totila's recovery; Rome lost twice
Narses: Busta Gallorum, Mons Lactarius, the Volturnus

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 540-562 (including the Lazic War)
wars.outcome: Fifty Years' Peace: Lazica Roman, Rome pays 30,000 nomismata a year
wars.summary: Khosrow I's invasion of Syria and sack of Antioch (540) opened twenty years of war: Mesopotamian campaigns until the truce of 545, and a long war in Lazica on the Black Sea coast (541-562).

phases.t: Mesopotamia and Syria: Antioch, Anglon, Edessa
Lazic War: Petra, Archaeopolis, Phasis
Truce and Fifty Years' Peace

wars.name: Roman intervention in Spain and the province of Spania
wars.outcome: Roman province of Spania held on the south-east coast for seventy years, finally lost to Suinthila
wars.summary: Justinian's expedition under Liberius in support of Athanagild, leaving a Roman coastal province that the Visigothic kings gradually reconquered.

wars.name: Roman-Lombard Wars
wars.outcome: Italy divided between the Lombard kingdom and duchies and the Roman exarchate
wars.summary: The Lombard invasion of 568 and the following decades of war, Roman diplomacy with the Franks, the creation of the exarchate, and papal negotiations with Agilulf, ending in truces after 598-605.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 572-591
wars.outcome: Roman intervention restores Khosrow II; Rome gains most of Armenia without payment
wars.summary: Justin II's war in support of the Armenian revolt and in alliance with the Turks; the loss of Dara drove him mad. Two decades of campaigns in Mesopotamia and Armenia ended when Maurice restored Khosrow II against Bahram Chobin.

wars.name: Avar and Slav Wars in the Balkans
wars.outcome: Roman victories beyond the Danube by 599-602, undone by the mutiny of 602 and the Persian war
wars.summary: From the Avar siege of Sirmium to the mutiny of 602: Avar raids, Slav settlement in the Balkans and Greece, and Maurice's offensives across the Danube after 591.

wars.name: Heraclian Revolt
wars.outcome: Phocas overthrown; Heraclius emperor
wars.summary: Civil war launched from Carthage by the exarch Heraclius the Elder, fought in Egypt and decided by the younger Heraclius's naval descent on Constantinople.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian War of 602-628
wars.outcome: Roman victory after near-collapse: Khosrow II overthrown; all lost territory and the True Cross restored; both empires exhausted
wars.summary: The 'last great war of antiquity'. Persia conquered Mesopotamia, Syria, Palestine and Egypt and reached the Bosporus; Heraclius counterattacked through Armenia and Azerbaijan, survived the Avar-Persian siege of Constantinople, and destroyed Khosrow's army at Nineveh.

phases.t: Persian conquest of Mesopotamia under Phocas
Fall of Syria, Palestine and Egypt; Persians at Chalcedon
Heraclius's campaigns in Armenia and Atropatene; siege of Constantinople
Turkic alliance, Nineveh, fall of Khosrow

wars.name: Arab conquest of the Roman Near East
wars.outcome: Syria, Palestine, Mesopotamia and Egypt lost; the empire reduced to Anatolia, the Balkan coasts, Africa and Italian enclaves (war continued after 641)
wars.summary: From the skirmish at Mu'ta (629) to the surrender of Babylon and the Treaty of Alexandria (641), the armies of Medina destroyed Roman power in the Near East: Dathin and Ajnadayn (634), Damascus (635), the Yarmuk (636), Jerusalem (637), Mesopotamia (639-640) and Egypt (639-641).

phases.t: First raids: Mu'ta, Tabuk
Conquest of Palestine and Syria: Dathin, Ajnadayn, Fahl, Damascus, Yarmuk
Jerusalem, northern Syria, Mesopotamia, Caesarea
Invasion of Egypt

campaigns.name: Lars Porsenna's march on Rome
campaigns.strength: unknown
campaigns.summary: Porsenna's army from Clusium came down the Chiana and Tiber valleys, seized the Janiculum and blockaded (or took) Rome; his son Arruns later pushed into Latium and was destroyed at Aricia.

path.note: Porsenna musters his army

path.t: Past Volsinii into the Tiber valley
Down the Tiber through Faliscan country

path.note: Veii regains the Septem Pagi under the peace

campaigns.note: Route reconstructed from geography; sources give only endpoints.

campaigns.name: Coriolanus' Volscian campaign
campaigns.strength: Volscian army (no figure)
campaigns.summary: Livy's list of the towns Coriolanus took on his march from Volscian country to the edge of Rome: Circeii, Satricum, Longula, Polusca, Corioli, Lavinium, then Corbio, Vetelia, Trebium, Labici and Pedum, before he camped at the Fossae Cluiliae.

path.t: Antium, Volscian base of Attius Tullius

path.note: Veturia and Volumnia persuade him to withdraw

campaigns.note: The list of towns may reflect real 5th-century Volscian conquests attached to a legendary figure.

campaigns.name: The Gallic march on Rome
campaigns.strength: perhaps 30,000 (Diodorus; guess)
campaigns.summary: The Senones crossed the Apennines from the Adriatic, besieged Clusium, then marched down the Tiber valley, routed the Romans at the Allia and sacked Rome; after seven months they departed with a ransom.

path.t: Down the Paglia and Tiber valleys
Sack of Rome; siege of the Capitol

path.note: Polybius: the Veneti had invaded their lands

campaigns.note: Varronian date 390; Polybius 387/386. Diodorus has the Gauls camp in Iapygia/Apulia after the sack; Strabo says Caere defeated them on their return.

campaigns.name: The Caudine Forks campaign
campaigns.strength: two consular armies, perhaps 20,000
campaigns.summary: The consuls concentrated at Calatia and, believing false reports that Luceria was besieged, took the short route through the Caudine pass toward Apulia, where Gavius Pontius trapped and forced the surrender of the whole army.

path.note: Samnite soldiers disguised as shepherds report Luceria under siege

path.t: Caudine Forks: army trapped and surrenders

path.note: Campanians give them clothing and arms

campaigns.note: Exact site of the Forks disputed (Arpaia-Montesarchio valley most favoured).

campaigns.name: Fabius Rullianus through the Ciminian forest
campaigns.strength: consular army, c. two legions plus allies
campaigns.summary: From Sutrium Fabius crossed the dense Ciminian forest by night, ravaged the untouched plains of central Etruria, defeated the Etruscans and brought Perusia, Cortona and Arretium to seek a truce.

path.t: Night march through the Ciminian forest
Ravaging the plains of central Etruria
Through the Chiana valley toward the northern cities

campaigns.note: Livy gives few topographical details beyond the forest and Perusia.

campaigns.name: The Sentinum campaign
campaigns.strength: four legions plus at least as many allies, c. 36,000-40,000
campaigns.summary: After a legion was destroyed near Camerinum, the consuls Fabius and Decius marched north through Umbria and crossed the Apennines to meet the Samnites and Senones at Sentinum, while diversionary attacks on Etruria drew off the Etruscans and Umbrians.

path.note: before the consuls' arrival

campaigns.note: Route inferred; Livy places the legion's destruction near Clusium, Polybius near Camerinum.

campaigns.name: Pyrrhus' Italian campaigns of 280-279
campaigns.strength: 20,000 foot, 3,000 horse, 2,000 archers, 500 slingers, 20 elephants (Plutarch), plus Tarentine and Italian allies
campaigns.summary: Pyrrhus crossed from Epirus, lost ships in a storm, won at Heraclea, marched up through Campania toward Rome as far as Anagnia or Praeneste, wintered at Tarentum and fought the costly victory at Ausculum in 279.

path.note: embarks in spring

path.t: Storm-scattered landing on the Messapian coast
Battle of Heraclea on the Siris

campaigns.note: Plutarch says he came within 300 stades of Rome; Eutropius and Florus name Praeneste.

campaigns.name: Pyrrhus in Sicily and his last Italian campaign (278-275)
campaigns.strength: c. 8,000 foot and elephants crossing to Sicily; 30,000 foot and 2,500 horse with Sicilian allies (Diodorus)
campaigns.summary: Pyrrhus crossed to Sicily, relieved Syracuse, swept the Carthaginians from all but Lilybaeum, failed to take it, lost Greek support, fought his way back to Italy through a Punic fleet, was checked at Beneventum and sailed home.

path.t: Back to Syracuse amid Greek disaffection
Naval defeat in the Strait of Messina

campaigns.note: Sicilian chronology follows Diodorus 22 and Plutarch 22-24.

campaigns.name: Alexander of Epirus in southern Italy
campaigns.strength: unknown; Epirote army with Tarentine support
campaigns.summary: Invited by Tarentum, Alexander campaigned against Messapians, Lucanians, Samnites and Bruttians, from Sipontum in Apulia to Paestum and Consentia, before being killed at Pandosia.

path.t: Victory near Paestum over Samnites and Lucanians

campaigns.note: Order of operations uncertain; Livy 8.17 and 8.24 and Justin 12.2 are brief.

campaigns.name: Regulus' invasion of Africa
campaigns.strength: 330 ships at Ecnomus; 15,000 foot and 500 horse left in Africa
campaigns.summary: The first Roman invasion of Africa: the fleet fought its way past the Carthaginian navy at Ecnomus, landed at Aspis, won at Adys and reached Tunes, before Xanthippus destroyed Regulus' army in spring 255.

path.note: embarks the army of both consuls
after crossing the Sicilian channel
peace talks fail
Regulus captured
evacuated by the fleet

campaigns.name: The Gallic invasion of 225
campaigns.strength: 50,000 foot and 20,000 horse and chariots (Polybius 2.23)
campaigns.summary: The Boii, Insubres and Gaesatae crossed the Apennines into Etruria, plundered as far as Clusium, defeated a praetorian army near Faesulae, and, retreating up the coast with their booty, were trapped between two consular armies at Telamon.

path.note: three days from Rome
Polybius' 'Faesulae' may be an error

campaigns.note: Polybius' topography (Faesulae north, Telamon south) is hard to reconcile; many scholars move the first battle to the Clusium area.

campaigns.name: Hannibal's march to Italy
campaigns.strength: c. 90,000 foot and 12,000 horse at the Ebro; 38,000 foot and 8,000 horse at the Rhône; 20,000 foot and 6,000 horse on arrival in Italy (Polybius 3.35, 3.56)
campaigns.summary: From New Carthage Hannibal marched across the Ebro and the Pyrenees, forced the Rhône, crossed the Alps in about fifteen days in October-November, took Turin and beat the Romans at the Ticinus and the Trebia.

path.note: departs in late spring
subdues the tribes north of the river; leaves Hanno with 10,000
probably near Le Perthus
negotiates passage with Gallic chiefs

path.t: Through the land of the Volcae

path.note: settles a dispute among the Allobroges
Allobroges attack on the ascent
route uncertain
Col du Clapier, Mont Cenis or Traversette

campaigns.note: Alpine pass disputed (Col de la Traversette, Col du Clapier, Mont Cenis, Mont Genèvre, Little St Bernard); the path drawn follows a Clapier route.

campaigns.name: Hannibal's campaigns of 217-216
campaigns.strength: c. 50,000 by 216 including Gallic allies
campaigns.summary: Leaving winter quarters in the Po valley, Hannibal crossed the Apennines and the flooded Arno marshes (losing an eye), destroyed Flaminius at Trasimene, marched to the Adriatic, ravaged Campania under Fabius' eyes, wintered at Gerunium and annihilated the Roman army at Cannae.

path.note: four days and three nights in water; Hannibal loses an eye

path.t: Ravages around Cortona to provoke Flaminius

path.note: Fabius shadows him

path.t: Ager Falernus and the oxen stratagem

campaigns.name: Hannibal's march on Rome
campaigns.strength: picked force, perhaps 30,000
campaigns.summary: To relieve Capua, Hannibal marched on Rome, camped by the Anio and rode to the Colline Gate, then withdrew, plundering the sanctuary of Feronia, when the besiegers of Capua stayed put. The route given follows Livy (from Coelius); Polybius sends him through Samnium.

path.t: Camp on the Anio; rides to the Colline Gate

campaigns.note: Polybius (9.5-7) and Livy (26.7-11) give different routes.

campaigns.name: Scipio's campaigns in Spain
campaigns.strength: c. 28,000 foot and 3,000 horse at New Carthage (Polybius); 45,000 foot and 3,000 horse at Ilipa
